nodes.summary: For a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the Boolean adjacency of $u$ and $v$ in $E$ is true exactly when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ occurs in $E$.
nodes.title: Edge-list adjacency for EDGE DOMINATING SET

nodes.summary: EDGE DOMINATING SET is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an EDGE DOMINATING SET instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and feasible, that is, some sublist of $E$ with at most $K$ entries contains, for every edge of $E$, an edge sharing an endpoint with it. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The EDGE DOMINATING SET decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance with vertex count $n$, edge list $E$ and bound $K$ is feasible when some sublist $D$ of $E$ (its entries taken in order) has at most $K$ entries and dominates every edge of $E$: for every $e \in E$ there is $d \in D$ such that one of the two entries of $d$ equals one of the two entries of $e$.
nodes.title: Feasible EDGE DOMINATING SET instances

nodes.summary: An instance of EDGE DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the vertex count), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edge list) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: EDGE DOMINATING SET instances

nodes.summary: The EDGE DOMINATING SET decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: EDGE DOMINATING SET is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance with vertex count $n$, edge list $E$ and bound $K$ is well formed when $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not occur in $E$. Thus $E$ lists the edges of a simple graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$, each once and in one orientation.
nodes.title: Well-formed EDGE DOMINATING SET instances
